summary: Test-only fix. The row `a diagram too large to draw in time shows the reason, and the page keeps responding @phone` (packages/dispatch/e2e/mermaid.e2e.ts:194) routes the shipped Mermaid worker chunk (/assets/mermaid-render.worker-<hash>.js) and serves it with one listener prepended that stops the worker's own listener, reports through an intercepted same-origin request (/e2e/mermaid-worker-held) that it holds the source, and never returns; the page's real 5 s limit then refuses it on every runner. The test asserts the hold report before sampling page timers, then the refusal text 'within 5 seconds', the source and no diagram. No executable line under web/src changes; timing comments in mermaid-diagrams.ts:73-76, packages/dispatch/AGENTS.md:293, the row's own comment and the pr2311 solution doc are corrected to the CI evidence. A2 in CI runs on a throwaway non-draft pull request from branch infra-713-negative-control (RENDER_TIME_LIMIT_MS = 600_000), so no push is held back and the issue PR's run is not cancelled.

rootCauseEvidence.observed: Runs 40692470398 and 40698817533: the row fails in chromium, iphone, webkit and firefox at mermaid.e2e.ts:232 (refusal status not found within 15 s). Run 40696018569: fails in chromium and iphone, passes in webkit and firefox at 6.8 s. Error-context snapshots of run 40692470398 (artifact dispatch-e2e-test-results-1) show img "Rendered Mermaid diagram" in the card in all four projects: the runner drew the 800-node diagram inside the 5 s limit.

T2 Rewrite the row in packages/dispatch/e2e/mermaid.e2e.ts:191-240: two page.route calls before goto (chunk: route.fetch + fulfill with the prepended listener; hold path: 204 and count), expect.poll on holds >= 1 with a message and loads >= 1 before the samples, keep the five 100 ms samples, toHaveCount(0), the exact refusal text, the n799 --> n0 source and no diagram; keep the title, @phone and the 800-node body; rewrite the row comment and header lines 4-10.

T3 Correct timing comments only: mermaid-diagrams.ts:73-76, packages/dispatch/AGENTS.md:293 (plus one sentence on how the row holds the worker), dated note in docs/solutions/dispatch-web/draw-untrusted-content-with-a-layout-engine-in-a-worker-whose-clock-starts-at-ready-pr2311.md.
T4 cd packages/dispatch && bun run lint && bun run typecheck && bun test web/src/features/refs.

T5 Pod proof: whole mermaid spec in chromium, iphone, webkit, firefox; -g 'too large to draw' --repeat-each=5; A2 control 1 (RENDER_TIME_LIMIT_MS = 600_000) and control 2 (window.setTimeout(noop, timeLimitMs) at mermaid-diagrams.ts:270) each fail at the refusal toHaveText; lapse L1 (non-matching chunk route fails at the hold poll) and L2 (a 2 s page-thread block fails a sample); A3 greps; restore and rebuild after each.

T6 Push the code head on legion/INFRA-713 and open the issue PR (Dispatch: INFRA-713); at once push the control commit (code head + 600_000) on branch infra-713-negative-control and open a non-draft control PR with no Dispatch line; subscribe to both PRs' Envoy topics and end the turn; quote the issue PR's four row ✓ lines and the control PR's four ✘ lines from the dispatch job log; close the control PR with --delete-branch and jj abandon the control commit.
T7 PR body E2E (implementer) with both CI runs and the pod runs; implement.json proof entries for A1 CI, A1 pod, A2, A3.

The job's overall status is not the evidence: recipients-claim.e2e.ts:310 (dispatch://INFRA-523) is red independently and dispatch is not a required check.

findings.finding: A CI negative control that removes the refusal never reaches the browser suite: MarkdownBody.test.tsx:1341-1353 unit-tests the refusal and the dispatch job's unit-test, lint and typecheck steps run first.
findings.answer: Decision 4: the control edit is RENDER_TIME_LIMIT_MS = 600_000, which passes lint, typecheck and every unit test (each sets its own limit) and disables the refusal for the row's whole 15 s window; the literal disable (window.setTimeout(noop, timeLimitMs)) runs on the pod only. Expected failure line: the refusal toHaveText, after the hold poll and samples passed.

findings.finding: 'On the same runner' in CI clashes with cancel-in-progress concurrency, 35-44 min runs, no workflow_dispatch, drafts running nothing, and the relayed rule never to hold back a push for a check; the dispatch job is red anyway from other rows.
findings.answer: Decision 5: the control runs on a second non-draft PR (branch infra-713-negative-control, outside legion/ so the daemon ignores it, no Dispatch line), pushed at the same time as the issue PR, so no push is held and neither run cancels the other; 'same runner' = same job on the same runner class (ubuntu-24.04). Evidence is the row's own ✓/✘ lines, never the job status.

findings.finding: The responsiveness half becomes nearly empty: a busy stub worker not blocking the page is the browser's guarantee.
findings.answer: The plan states the app-level claim: the page hands the source to the worker chunk and stays responsive while that worker is busy with it; a page drawing on its own thread never loads the chunk and fails at the hold assertion; samples are taken only after the hold report. Lapse L2 (a 2 s page-thread block) shows the samples can fail. A real diagram no runner can finish was rejected as speed-dependent by construction and capped by the 32,000-character body limit.

findings.finding: With the stub, size does not matter, and an 800-node body could let a slow pod's real draw produce the refusal for the wrong reason; the title names the size.
findings.answer: Decision 2: title and body stay (spec A1 and the pr2311 solution doc name the row by title; the full source is asserted). The hold report is asserted before any refusal assertion and only the prepended listener (which stops the real one) sends it, so the refusal can only come from the timer; lapse L1 proves the hold assertion fires.

findings.finding: Comments and docs state false timing facts: mermaid.e2e.ts:191-193 ('over a minute'), header :8-10, mermaid-diagrams.ts:73-76, AGENTS.md:293 ('only a diagram far past what a comment holds meets the limit'), the pr2311 solution doc ('passes in four engines'); the spec Summary is contradicted by run 40696018569.
findings.answer: Decision 6 / T2-T3 correct each (comment and doc text only). The spec Summary inaccuracy is reported to the architect; acceptance is unaffected and the spec is left as it is.

findings.finding: The 5 s timer starts at postMessage, before the hold report; a bare await on the report hangs to the 30 s test timeout with no message.
findings.answer: T2: expect.poll on the hold count, bounded by the 15 s expect timeout, with a message. The samples take about 0.6-1 s, well inside the 5 s window; the pod run in WebKit measures it.

findings.finding: Exact counts of one worker load and one hold report may flake when dropAbandoned starts a fresh worker (iPhone Thread dialog, refetch); the spike did not cover the real chunk, terminate(), iphone or the Go server's headers.
findings.answer: Decision 3: counts are asserted as at least one and the observed counts are recorded per project; the first pod run covers the four untested points, and a failure there is a design signal reported to the architect.

findings.finding: A3 needs a machine check; resetMermaidDiagrams is an existing test-only seam in shipped code.
findings.answer: Decision 8 and T5's A3 commands: comment-only diff under web/src, RENDER_TIME_LIMIT_MS = 5000, resetMermaidDiagrams imported only by MarkdownBody.test.tsx and never exposed to window, URL or page content; the exact text 'within 5 seconds' pins the shipped value.

findings.finding: The pod run needs exact commands: harness, DATABASE_URL on loopback, wkenv.sh, rebuilds after each control edit and restore, lines to quote.
findings.answer: T1 and T5 give them, citing the INFRA-42, INFRA-43, INFRA-95 and LEGION-695 solution docs.

findings.finding: Serving a changed body for an app asset is a new e2e pattern; AGENTS.md says not to replace the server with a fixture server; the route depends on Vite's default worker file name.
findings.answer: Decision 1: the real server serves the real chunk; the test only prepends a listener, as deep-links.e2e.ts:555 already routes a built chunk. AGENTS.md:293 gains one sentence on it. The load/hold assertions come before the refusal assertions, so a renamed chunk fails with the hold poll's message.

findings.finding: Changelog: does a test-only change earn a fragment?
findings.answer: Decision 7: no fragment; nothing a user or operator meets changes. The sjawhar/legion#2311 fragment stays true.

findings.finding: Overall: A1 met by design, checkable only from row lines; A2 needs the CI answers; A3 met once the existing hook is addressed; responsiveness meaning open.
findings.answer: Answered by decisions 3-5 and 8 and the responsiveness claim above.

specDepartures.spec: Change: 'For example, the test lowers the limit through a test-only hook the page reads, or it draws a diagram that no runner can finish within the limit while page timers keep arriving.'
specDepartures.plan: Neither example. The test routes the shipped worker chunk and prepends a listener that holds the source forever, so the page's shipped 5 s limit refuses it on every runner; no page hook is added.
specDepartures.evidence: A lowered limit makes the samples and the refusal fight over speed again; a bigger diagram is speed-dependent and capped by the 32,000-character body limit. Spike on the pod (Playwright 1.63.0, chromium/firefox/webkit): the route intercepts the module worker's script and the worker's own fetch in all three engines, the real listener never answers, and a 100 ms page timer fires in 100-120 ms.

specDepartures.spec: A2: 'with the refusal disabled in the page code (restored afterwards), the row fails on the same runner.'
specDepartures.plan: In CI the refusal is disabled by RENDER_TIME_LIMIT_MS = 600_000 on a throwaway control pull request (branch infra-713-negative-control) whose run goes beside the issue PR's on the same job and runner class; on the pod both that edit and the literal window.setTimeout(noop, timeLimitMs) run.
specDepartures.evidence: MarkdownBody.test.tsx:1341-1353 unit-tests the refusal and the dispatch job's unit-test step runs before the browser step, so a literal removal never reaches Playwright in CI; envoy-and-contracts.yaml concurrency (keyed by PR number, cancel-in-progress) would cancel a red run on the issue PR at the restore push; GitHub-hosted runners are fresh VMs per job.
